records.claim: Treasury Policy v3, board-approved 2025-04-22, says it supersedes v1 and v2. s.4.1 reads: 'Hedge 75% of each confirmed foreign-currency receivable above USD 1M equivalent with maturity of 12 months or less, using forward contracts.'
records.applicability: Sets the hedge ratio (75%) and instrument (forwards) for the EUR 8M receivable: 75% x EUR 8M = EUR 6M.
records.limitations: Supplied document. It has not been checked against board minutes or governance records. The file is a short excerpt, so other sections such as definitions and counterparty limits are not visible.

records.claim: Policy v3 s.4.2: 'Hedge ratios are not to be varied based on management's views of future exchange rates.'
records.applicability: Rules out the treasurer's plan to stay unhedged because she expects the euro to strengthen.
records.limitations: Excerpt only. It does not say how 'views' would be judged in practice.

records.claim: Policy v3 s.4.3: 'Deviations require Audit Committee approval.'

records.claim: The sign of the forward premium is consistent with covered interest parity. USD rates (3.75-4.00%) are above EUR rates (deposit 2.50%), so EUR/USD should trade at a forward premium to spot, as the quote shows (1.1810 vs 1.1650). As a rough check, the quoted premium is about 1.4% over about 263 days, roughly 1.9% annualised. That is somewhat above the ~1.25-1.5pp policy-rate gap, so the bank's points may include a margin or reflect term-rate expectations.
records.applicability: Supports the conclusion that the forward premium reflects interest-rate differentials, not an expected euro rise. It also flags that the bank's pricing should be checked against the live forward.
records.limitations: Approximate arithmetic using policy rates rather than matched-tenor EUR/USD OIS or deposit rates. Day count is approximate. Both central banks were reported as hiking, so term rates may differ. Recompute from live data.

verification.method: Reasoned from retrieved figures; no live term rates obtained

records.claim: Covered interest parity is a no-arbitrage identity that links forward points to the interest-rate differential. The forward rate is not an unbiased predictor of future spot (the forward premium / Fama puzzle), and forward rates have little power to forecast spot.

source.title: CFA Institute: Currency Exchange Rates: Understanding Equilibrium Value (2026)

records.applicability: The 1.1810 forward is a price set by rate differentials, not a market forecast that the euro will rise.
records.limitations: Search snippets only. One cited paper suggests the sign of the Fama coefficient changed after the GFC.

records.claim: Meese and Rogoff (1983) found that a random walk forecasts major dollar exchange rates out of sample as well as structural and time-series models at 1 to 12 month horizons. Later work largely confirms this for point-forecast accuracy (RMSE). Some studies find an edge on directional accuracy or at longer horizons.
records.applicability: The horizon here is about 7 months, inside the 1-12 month range studied. Supports the conclusion that a June 2027 point forecast cannot reliably drive the decision.
records.limitations: The original studies used 1970s data and other currency pairs (USD/DEM, not EUR). Search snippets only.

records.claim: As a group, professional and analyst exchange-rate forecasters generally do not beat naive random-walk forecasts. Few individual forecasters do, and many do significantly worse. There are some exceptions, for example Chilean peso survey forecasts at 2 months.
records.applicability: Bank or consensus point forecasts for June 2027 should not be treated as reliable.
records.limitations: Snippets only. No study found directly compares EUR/USD consensus forecasts with the forward. A secondary summary (daytrading.com) claims some skill in 2-year-ahead forecasts, which is not verified.

records.claim: Short-horizon EUR/USD forecasts vary widely. Two automated forecast sites projected end-November 2026 levels of about 1.068 and about 1.131. Commentary describes EUR/USD as caught between two central banks that are both hiking.
records.applicability: Shows how widely forecasts disagree. It is not evidence of where the rate will be.
records.limitations: Single search summary. The second site was not clearly identified. Model outputs of low quality.

records.claim: Under ASC 815, hedge designation and documentation must be in place at inception. A hedged forecasted transaction must be probable within the documented hedge period. A FX receivable can be hedged with a single cash flow hedge covering settlement of the receivable, or with a cash flow hedge of the forecasted sale followed by a fair value hedge once the receivable is recognised. Forward points may be excluded from the effectiveness assessment.

source.title: Deloitte DART 5.3 Foreign Currency Cash Flow Hedges

records.applicability: If the company wants hedge accounting, documentation must be done before or when the forward is executed.
records.limitations: Search snippets only, mostly from one domain (Deloitte). The full codification was not inspected. The company's accounting policy and GAAP election are unknown.
